original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a bounded nonempty closed subset of U. Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. Fact 4.4 says that if f is also supercoercive, then the left farthest-point map Q_left,C is single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is supercoercivity actually necessary for that almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness result?
target_in_paper: Problem 6 in Section 8: "Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 4.4 really essential?" This is the paper's exact open problem corresponding to your draft, and it is foreshadowed immediately after Fact 4.4 in Section 4. refined_question: Let X = R^n, let f : X -> (-infinity,+infinity] be a Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed bounded subset of U. Define the Bregman distance by D_f(x,y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x-y> for y in U, and define the left Bregman farthest-point map by Q_left,C(y) = {x in C : D_f(x,y) = sup_{c in C} D_f(c,y) < +infinity}. Assume that f is twice continuously differentiable on U and that grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. Is the supercoercivity assumption on f in Fact 4.4 actually necessary for the conclusion that Q_left,C is single-valued on U outside a meager Lebesgue-null subset of U? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: Your draft is targeting the exact open problem the authors isolate as Problem 6. Section 4 states Fact 4.4, immediately says that it would be interesting to know whether supercoercivity is essential there, and Section 8 repeats that question verbatim as Problem 6. This is narrower than the neighboring Theorem 4.3, which removes supercoercivity for a different statement (left Klee sets themselves), and different from Corollary 4.5, which gives a dual full-domain statement for the right farthest-point map. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
